cadet.crisis.apollo13.onsetLead: It is April 1970. On the way to the Moon, an oxygen tank burst. The 3 astronauts moved into the Moon lander, Aquarius, to stay safe. It was built for 2 people for about 2 days. Now it must keep 3 people safe for almost 4 days.
cadet.crisis.apollo13.onsetDetail: Carbon dioxide, a gas people breathe out, is building up in the air. Filters take it out. But Aquarius's round filters are used up. The spare filters in the other spaceship are square. They do not fit. The gas keeps rising slowly. Can you find a fix in time?
cadet.crisis.spe1972.onsetLead: In August 1972, the Sun sent out one of the biggest radiation storms ever seen in the space age. It came between two Moon missions, so no one was in the storm. Scientists say astronauts outside on the Moon would have been in great danger.
cadet.crisis.spe1972.onsetDetail: In this mission, you imagine it happens now. Your crew is outside, exploring. Space radiation can hurt people who are not protected. Get everyone into the shelter with thick walls, fast.
cadet.crisis.mirFire.onsetLead: It is February 1997, on the old space station Mir. A machine that makes oxygen caught fire in one room. Flames and smoke spread. The fire blocked the way to one of the escape ships.
cadet.crisis.mirFire.onsetDetail: Smoke that is bad to breathe is filling the station. The crew put on masks and use fire extinguishers on the flames. Can you put out the fire and keep everyone safe?

specialist.crisis.apollo13.onsetLead: Service Module Oxygen Tank 2 ruptured at 55h 55m elapsed mission time. The crew shut down Odyssey and evacuated to the Lunar Module Aquarius as an emergency lifeboat. Built for 2 astronauts for ~45 hours, Aquarius must now sustain 3 astronauts across an 87-hour (~3.6-day) translunar return trajectory [A13-CO2].
specialist.crisis.apollo13.onsetDetail: Aquarius’s round LiOH scrubbers are exhausted. The Command Module carries abundant square LiOH canisters, but they do not fit the LM receptacles. Cabin ppCO₂ is climbing steadily at ~0.31 mmHg/hr toward lethal hypercapnia (15.0 mmHg peak historical ceiling).
specialist.crisis.spe1972.onsetLead: Between Apollo 16 and Apollo 17, no astronauts were on the lunar surface. This historical 'what-if' simulation places a 3-person surface crew at an Apollo-era outpost during the extreme August 1972 solar particle event. Two astronauts are caught on EVA when shock-accelerated proton flux begins delivering >0.5 Gy over several hours [HRP-ARS].
specialist.crisis.spe1972.onsetDetail: Two crew members are caught on EVA with spacesuit shielding of only 0.3 g/cm². Unshielded surface dose rates exceed >0.5 Gy over several hours [HRP-ARS] (~0.5 Gy over the 6-hour peak), which causes acute radiation sickness without shelter. Immediate evacuation to the regolith storm shelter (20 g/cm²) keeps acute dose under the 250 mSv 30-day limit [OCHMO-RAD].
specialist.crisis.mirFire.onsetLead: During evening preparation, a lithium perchlorate solid-fuel oxygen generation candle (Vika / TGK) ruptured inside Kvant-1. Molten metal and pressurized oxygen created a blowtorch flame spraying against the aluminum hull and filling the modules with dense, choking black smoke.
specialist.crisis.mirFire.onsetDetail: The flame blocked the hatchway to one of the docked Soyuz return craft, threatening the crew's emergency escape path. The cosmonauts and astronauts must battle zero-gravity fireballs using 3 foam/water extinguishers while donning respirators in pitch darkness.
